key_insight: TCA-SIR reframes scientific inspiration retrieval as learning a transferable, target-conditioned abstraction rather than just ranking papers by topical similarity.
engineering_relevance: For AI-for-Science systems, this enables retrieval of sources that better support hypothesis generation by explicitly modeling how a candidate’s mechanism can transfer to the target problem.
method: Generate a target-conditioned abstraction from each candidate source paper.
Represent the abstraction and use it to predict transferability to the target.
Use the learned abstraction both for retrieval ranking and for interpretable rationale generation.
evidence_signal: On ResearchBench, TCA-SIR outperforms prior SIR methods and direct LLM retrieval, improving HitRate@top4% over MOOSE-Chem by more than 10 percentage points.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of learned abstractions, so noisy or weak target conditioning could reduce transferability ranking reliability.
paper_title: TCA-SIR: Learning Target-Conditioned Abstractions for Scientific Inspiration Retrieval
